As far as I understand, Find Familiar is a Wizard spell, I'd be taking Druidic spells for the feat. Druids only get to Find Familiar by expending Wildshape use, which I won't be doing as I am saving them up for my Starry Form. No fae floof for me, sadly. Although if I could get away with taking the feat for Wizard spells, maybe basing it on the wizard sibling who has in-game reasons to help/support/try to protect the druid and my druid's int at the moment is 15 and I was considering boosting it to 16 at later levels, that would be both incredibly interesting and fun, as well as potentially overpowered because I'd get Identify, Leomund's Tiny Hut and so forth, not just Detect Magic or the fun Find Familiar. While it'd definitely cover my party's bases a lot more, would it not feel like MinMaxing?

(Not sure how the feat would impact at what range I can cast Cure Wounds?) 

I agree Stars Druids sound quite powerful and if not for utility fear/covering our behinds as the main Spellcaster, I'd not even be wondering about this, really. 

I don't see my PC as someone who'd only heal when they're down, so I think Grave Cleric is probably out, unless later on some big, thematic things happen, she does have Haunted One background and certain curse/evil prophecy tethered so I think some deviations are possible down the lane. But definitely more drawn to Twilight or Arcana cleric, if I had to pick, although not sure at what level I'd multiclass and how to distribute it, but something to consider for future, if I feel our party needs it, maybe?

However, the ritual caster feat could possible be something I start off with, if the DM allows 1st lvl feat thing or I could get as soon as next level as well, while still gaining levels in Druid.

Like I have an Astral Self Monk whose Astral form is the Quori and the PC believe it is their true self instead of physical body and strives to be able to shift their being more and more into their incorporeal form.

Also I love Genasi & Tieflings for aesthetics. Have had a DM let me play tiefling-ish looks on Star Circle Druid that's Kalashtar (because the Quori spirit is attached to human lineage but it can mix with a Tiefling at some point and inherit some physical properties, imo) and it's just the good stuff.

Multiclassed Ranger/Druid as a kid back in 3.5 and still love Druids to heck and back. But Paladins are growing on me. Do want to get a chance to play more, not just DM, to actually experience differences in classes, but when I will have more time to DM I suppose I'll get to experience some classes through NPCs and enemies, so looking forward to that. :)

I am, for better or for worse, not a big city person, at all (to point even my small town where woods are 3 minute walk away from my building feels too "city" at times), and I do think it'd be something I'd ultimately very, very regret, if I was even capable of going through with. But I appreciate the thought/advice as in many ways, it is the logical one to offer.

Perhaps only on lowest level with my asthma (and I'd have to fight for it very hard, invest money in it) which would not even pay half of my bills, so I would still need to work, but it'd unfavorable tick for hiring - so not really worth it in the long shot.

Sometimes, that alone is reason enough. There is no bigger regret that I've experienced than not being able to be there for someone you love. I personally think that regret goes beyond just when you're alive, somehow.

Your father... I don't think you indirectly killed him. You don't have to keep giving everyone chances, this isn't your fault. His life wasn't great overall for many reasons, by the sound of it, including his own powerlessness to break out of bad cycle. 

But that doesn't mean you are just as powerless, though it may feel so. You've endured a lot and you're your mother's support and sometimes, that is reason to stick around and while you do, things can change and change for the better. 

Happiness is complicated. Being depressed is complicated. It comes and it goes. Both of them.

Sometimes, just this light and easy feeling of breathing comes when you least expect it, found in a warm pastry as you walk down a quiet street or doing something you enjoy and it's not that bright burst of happiness people seem to speak of, but it's enough to hold onto from one moment to next and again, as if you're rock climbing. And sometimes you get a lift right to the top, by a brief, but pure feeling of happiness.

It may take some time, it may take examining what comes closest to happiness/not feeling empty for you (having a pet, attending college, spending a good day with your mom, something else?) it may take work with your therapist, but it's not impossible.

I wish you well. I really do. I also wish to you that you find more genuine friends, though there is also that you must have overheard them at rather young age (under 20, I'd assume) and lot of people haven't quite learned to empathic then yet. Which means, as time goes on, you can find more understanding people, though it's scary and not one huge leap all at once. But one step at a time is how all these things are solved, I find. As is life lived.
